title: Publish straight into the app's database
goal: Remove the duplicate: publish builds from the pipeline's base tables and goes directly to the app's database, so sllaw-etl stops holding a second copy of the corpus (it hit Neon Free's 1 GB limit 2026-11-18; the full republish after cf8ebae failed with DiskFull) (user).
for_whom: The nightly pipeline (it must publish again) and the lawyers using the app (the corpus they search must stay whole and current).

done_check.check: publish --apply writes kb.docs, kb.chunks and kb.links into schema kb of the database `app` in Neon sllaw-app, built from sllaw-etl's base tables (docs, chunks, mentions, links, same_as); the pipeline's role there can write only schema kb; the app reads kb read-only.
kb.mentions is not published (nothing in the app reads it); why a citation did not resolve stays in sllaw-etl's mentions table.

Before writing, publish measures the app database's size plus the release it is about to write; if that would pass 900 MB it stops with a message naming both numbers and writes nothing (the chats live in that database).

The pending full republish (12,275 documents) lands in one transaction: row counts in the app's kb equal what the base tables yield (docs 12,275; chunks and links counted the same way), and the app sees the old release until commit.
embed reads kb from the app's database; chunks whose id and text hash are unchanged are not re-embedded (count of re-embedded chunks reported).

The app (local and Vercel production) reads kb from its own database; a law page, a gazette and a judgment the app already shows return the same sections and links via the query the app's view runs; /coverage counts match kb.
sllaw-etl's schema kb is dropped and its bloated work tables compacted (VACUUM FULL); its size is reported before and after (978 MB now, target under 550 MB).
The nightly Dagster run on ampere passes end to end (publish and embed green).

scenarios.steps: After the move, run the app view's query for an amended section of an Act (e.g. one the citation chips open) against the app's kb.
scenarios.expect: Same text parts and the same amending links as the release before the move.

scenarios.steps: Run publish in memory/test with a size limit set below what the release needs.
scenarios.expect: It stops before writing, with both sizes in the message; the app's kb is unchanged.

scenarios.steps: Nightly run after a builder change that re-fingerprints every document.
scenarios.expect: Full republish fits (about 20 MB app data + 2 x ~300 MB at the peak, ~620 MB, under 900 MB) and commits in one go.

out_of_scope: Publishing in batches (the release stays one transaction).
Moving any Neon project to a paid plan.
Changing the build fingerprint so a builder edit stops rebuilding every document.
App features or UI; the app changes only where it connects to read kb.

decisions.note: Reverses 2026-11-08 'no separate app copy': kb lives in the app's database, sllaw-etl keeps only the pipeline's tables (user).
The app maps only kb.docs, kb.chunks, kb.links; kb.mentions (135 MB) has no reader, so it is not published.
kb.links keeps its context snippet (39 MB): with kb.mentions gone it is the only copy the app can read.
Rows now leave sllaw-etl (Neon egress): a full republish sends ~300 MB of the 5 GB monthly Free egress; nightly publishes send only changed documents.

Done by hand at the user's word before the build: sllaw-app's `neondb` (v1 corpus, 238 MB, read by nothing) and sllaw-etl's kb.mentions dropped; sllaw-app now holds `app` 10 MB, sllaw-etl 843 MB. publish still recreates kb.mentions until d2.
Recommended options taken after the user skipped the question round and said continue; the user corrects them at sign-off.

progress.note: Dropped by the user before sign-off ('no moving'); the waste in sllaw-etl is audited instead.
